---
title: "is.null() does not detect empty vectors"
ref: LEN-05
categories: [Empty and NA]
impact: incoherent
extrait: 'is.null(integer(0))'
reponse: 'FALSE'
attendu: "`TRUE`, the result is empty"
versions: "All"
source: "Slack ThinkR (2021, 2022)"
---

::: {.piege}
```{r}
found <- which(c(FALSE, FALSE))
found
is.null(found)

nothing <- unlist(list())
nothing
is.null(nothing)
length(nothing)
```
:::

## Why

`NULL` is an object of its own: the absence of an object. `integer(0)`, `character(0)` or `list()` are real, typed vectors that happen to have zero elements. `is.null()` only recognises the former.

Depending on the function, an empty result comes in one form or the other: `which()` returns `integer(0)`, `unlist(list())` and `c()` return `NULL`. An `is.null()` test therefore lets half of the empty cases through. The only thing they share: `length()` is 0 in both.

## The fix

Test the length, which covers `NULL` as well as empty vectors.

::: {.piege}
```{r}
length(found) == 0
length(nothing) == 0
```
:::
